speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning following a rear-end collision. Can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned and whether you are able to bear any weight on it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Is the right leg externally rotated and shortened compared to the left, and can you feel any numbness or tingling in your right foot?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: That specific positioning—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is highly characteristic of a posterior hip dislocation. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray
